canonical_topic: Options on forwards/futures deliver the contract, not the physical commodity
definition: Most energy options are written on forward or futures contracts, so exercising the option (even early) hands over the forward/futures position rather than the underlying physical commodity.
core_idea: Because the deliverable of an energy option is a forward or futures contract, early exercise only trades the option for the forward — actual physical delivery, if any, still waits for that forward's own expiration.
key_points: Exercising an option on a forward delivers the forward contract itself, not the physical commodity.
Any eventual physical delivery only occurs later, at the underlying forward contract's expiration.
This structure reduces the practical value of exercising an option early.
trading_implications: Early exercise rarely helps since it only swaps the option for the underlying forward, not for the physical commodity itself.
caveats: Assuming exercising a futures option triggers immediate physical delivery.
